newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down, institutions sell.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down, institutions sell.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down sharply on Monday after institutional selling in shares expected to post poor 1997 interim results in line with solid falls in A shares, brokers said.
The B index shed 1.349 points, or 1.78 percent, to 74.285 points on volume of 11.882 million shares worth $4.011 million, compared with $5.670 million on Friday.
The A index slipped 30.643 points, or 2.50 percent, to 1,193.397 on turnover of 3.29 billion yuan, against 3.4 billion yuan on Friday.

Brokers said that during the reporting season, many investors were concerned about the interim results of listed firms, which should be issued by the end of August. Some selling to unwind positions as a result of this caution depressed the market, they said.
"The weaker A share market also helped to sicken B share market sentiment," one broker said. "And more overseas selling today dragged the index down," he said.
"Market leaders, Pudong real estate shares, perfomed poorly recently on concerns about their interim results, which also hurt investors' buying interest," another broker said.
Of 45 B shares, 38 traded, with 29 down, five flat and four up.
Shanghai Huili Building Material Co was the biggest loser on speculative selling, tumbling $0.018 or 8.25 percent to $0.200 on thin volume of 2,000 shares.

Shanghai Erfangji Co was the most actively traded on institutional liquidation amid concerns over the possiblity it could show poor interim results. It fell $0.006 or 5.66 percent to $0.100 on volume of 1.1 million shares.

Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the second most actively traded on domestic selling also on expectations of unpromising interim results, down $0.030 or 2.43 percent to $1.200 on volume of 806,600 shares.

Shanghai's A share index continued to fall as market sentiment was weak and many institutional investors, jittery about the possiblity that further market-cooling measures would be introduced, were seen liquidating their positions, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index slumped 125.260 points or 3.37 percent to 3,596.439 points.
Shanghai United Holding Co was the biggest loser on institutional selling, diving 1.41 yuan or 9.03 percent to 14.20 yuan on volume of 1.6 million shares.
